Yes, guanine may be used as a colorant in pearlescent nail polish, provided that the product is externally applied and contains diluents only as specified in §73.1001(b) and nitrocellulose for externally applied cosmetics [5]. The use of guanine is permitted in cosmetics generally, including externally applied products such as nail polish, with no specific amount or concentration limits beyond good manufacturing practice. Guanine may be used in mixtures that contain diluents only if those diluents are listed under §73.1001(b) and nitrocellulose for external use [5]. The provisions do not specify any restriction on the amount of guanine, but its use is limited to formulations where diluents comply with the restrictions in §73.2329(a)(2)(ii) [5]. The definition of "area of the eye" includes eyelids, eyebrow, skin below the eyebrow, conjunctival sac, and soft tissue within the infra-orbital ridge; this applies to products applied near the eyes but does not restrict use in nail polish since nail polish is not applied in that area [9].

21 CFR 70.3(s) defines the "area of the eye" as including the eyelids, eyebrow, skin below the eyebrow, conjunctival sac, and soft areolar tissue within the infra-orbital ridge [9].  
21 CFR 73.2329(a) requires that guanine shall conform in identity and specifications to the requirements of §73.1329(a)(1) and (b) [1].  
21 CFR 73.2329(a)(1) requires that guanine used as a color additive must meet the identity and specification standards set forth in §73.1329(a)(1) and (b) [2].  
21 CFR 73.2329(a)(2) allows for color additive mixtures of guanine to contain diluents, with specific restrictions depending on product type [3].  
21 CFR 73.2329(a)(2)(i) limits the use of diluents in coloring cosmetics generally to those listed under §73.1001(a)(1) [4].  
21 CFR 73.2329(a)(2)(ii) restricts diluents for externally applied cosmetics to those listed in §73.1001(b) and, in addition, nitrocellulose [5].  
21 CFR 73.2329(b) permits the use of guanine in cosmetics generally, including those intended for use in the area of the eye, provided amounts are consistent with good manufacturing practice [6].  
21 CFR 73.2329(c) requires that any color additive or mixture prepared therefrom intended solely or in part for coloring purposes shall bear labeling in accordance with §70.25 [7].  
21 CFR 73.2329(d) exempts guanine from certification because it is deemed safe and does not require certification under section 721(c) of the act [8].
